chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Talbiyah of the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj), when does he cease it? He said: 'When you see the houses of Mecca.' And he ceases the Talbiyah for Hajj at the time of the sun's decline on the Day of Arafah. And he ceases the Talbiyah of the Mutamatti' Umrah when the camels' hooves touch the ground in the Haram. And we have explained that at the beginning of the Book of Hajj, and we have exhausted what is in it, so there is no need to repeat it in that regard.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّع: A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, in a single journey
key_terms.تَلْبِيَة: Ritual proclamation of 'Labbayk' (Here I am) recited during Hajj and Umrah
key_terms.زَوَال الشَّمْس: Decline of the sun (time for Dhuhr prayer)

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim stop reciting the Talbiyah during Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the precise moments for terminating the Talbiyah, distinguishing between the Umrah al-Mufradah, which ceases when the camel's hooves touch the ground in the Haram, and the Hajj Talbiyah, which concludes at solar noon on the Day of Arafah. This distinction highlights the ritual purity required upon entering the sacred precincts versus the specific timing of the Arafah stand, reflecting the detailed jurisprudential (fiqh) methodology of the Ahl al-Bayt in regulating pilgrimage rites.
